messages:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — FinCap (pilot) just confirmed they need a 99th pct latency SLO of ~200ms for chat completions. They said it'd unlock a paid tier. We need to pick sequencing for next quarter: invest primarily in a hotpath low-latency route (fast model sharding, KV cache prioritization, tail mitigation) OR push throughput/cost work (aggressive batching + int8 quant + cache warming). I sketched a tiny RICE to start the convo. Thoughts?

Sanjay (Eng): tl;dr: both matter but different customers. Hotpath is high-risk/medium-effort, big impact for premium users. Batch+quant is lower-risk, benefits everyone (cost savings). Quick RICE draft: Reach=2 (pilot customers), Impact=8, Confidence=6, Effort=5 -> RICE~192 for hotpath. For batch/quant: Reach=10, Impact=4, Confidence=7, Effort=6 -> RICE~280. (numbers rough)

Ellie (ML): Agree with Sanjay's framing. Also: hotpath improvements are more about tail distribution engineering (tail-aware batching, priority queues, prefetching KV) — that means new metrics (p99.9/p99.99) and more infra changes. For batch+quant we can run offline evals: quality drift with int8, latency vs token-length tradeoffs. Suggest parallel experiments: 1) canary hotpath for premium customers, 2) offline quant eval + controlled A/B for general traffic.

Patrick (SRE): SRE notes: hotpath routing will add more operational surface (two concurrent serving stacks, fast fallback). We need explicit rollout criteria: warm cache hit >= 70% on hotpath, p99 < 200ms for 95% of requests in canary window, and graceful fallback latency <500ms. Autoscaler settings must handle bursty premium traffic. If we run both tracks, prepare runbooks for fallback and rollback.

Jordan (Sales): To add context from FinCap: they said "we can commit to a paid pilot if p99 <=200ms for 2 weeks" and they're ok with a small premium. This is revenue + logo if we hit it. They also told me cost is secondary for them — they'd pay for reliability/latency.

Maya (PM): Proposed sequencing: Week 0-2: engineering spike for hotpath feasibility + finalize SLOs and runbooks. Week 3-6: parallel offline quant experiments and batching perf tuning. Week 7-8: canary hotpath for FinCap (small %). Launch criteria for completing the initiative: (1) FinCap canary p99 <= 200ms for 14 days, (2) no >10% increase in token cost for standard users (batch/quant improvements should offset), (3) runbook validated (failover < 2m). If we can't hit (1) without breaking (2), escalate to Exec.

Sanjay (Eng): Implementation note: hotpath approach = prioritized KV cache + short-seq optimized kernels + lightweight routing. Rough effort: 2 engineers full-time for 6 weeks to get canary. For batch/quant, a combined Eng+ML sprint of 4 weeks for measurable cost wins. Can do both if we split team (one focused on hotpath spike + canary, other on quant experiments).

Ellie (ML): Quality gating for int8: we should run prompt/regression suites (FinCap prompt set + general corpus). If quality delta > 1.5% absolute on key metrics, fail. Will set up eval jobs in CI.

Patrick (SRE): +1 to parallel path. Need explicit metric dashboards: p50/p95/p99/p99.9, tail error rate, cache hit ratio, autoscale latency. Also need SLA page for FinCap.

Maya (PM): Ok — decision: we sequence both in parallel with prioritization on hotpath canary for FinCap. Immediate asks: Sanjay - scope spike + canary plan by Mon; Ellie - quant/regression test matrix by Wed; Patrick - dashboards & runbook template by Fri; Jordan - lock FinCap pilot dates + commitment. I'll update the roadmap doc and create canary ticket. Please :thumbsup: if you agree or :thinking_face: if concerns.

rollout-bot: Canary job scheduled for 1719870000 (placeholder) once canary ticket is created.

Jordan (Sales): :thumbsup: FinCap tentatively good with dates. I'll confirm after we have a canary window.

Sanjay (Eng): :thumbsup: starting spike Monday.

Ellie (ML): :thumbsup: will post eval matrix in #eng-ml.

Patrick (SRE): :thumbsup: will stub dashboards and runbook.
